_comment: COMPUTE-MATCHED depth vs width on dyck1 -- the same pair as
compute-matched.json, on a rung that can actually test depth.
MOTIVATION. Every architecture experiment in this repo has run on
subst-fst-fixed and nothing else (all six arms resolve to pool instances:
320 = per_cell 160 x 2 tracks). On that rung the held-out answer is 'apply a
map already in your weights', which needs STORAGE of the rule, not
arithmetic to apply it. Three measurements say the rung is
storage-limited: the k axis shows demos are unused (0.909 -> 0.519 given one
demo), depth 1 sits BELOW the 0.333 chance rate in-distribution (0.201), and
the params-free pair showed the looped arm memorizing nothing at all (gap
-0.000). So 'depth loses' is untested rather than established.
dyck1 fixes that without writing a new task. The answer is
")".repeat(open_depth(input)) -- a function of the input's stack state, so
no memorized map can shortcut it. And the held-out prefixes are 8..28 chars
against demo prefixes of 2..10, so the sequential computation required grows
~3-14x at test time. That gradient is the depth probe.
THE PAIR (from examples/param_match.rs, not by hand):
looping : n_stages 4,  max_loops 8, d_model 128, ffn 384, head_dim 16
= 32 block-steps/token, 919,172 params
wide    : n_stages 32, max_loops 1, d_model  64, ffn  58, head_dim 16
= 32 block-steps/token, 919,648 params  (+0.05%)
Known uncontrolled difference, carried over from the subst-fst pair: head
COUNT is 8 vs 4 and cannot be matched at an 8x stage ratio. head_dim is
matched at 16. If the wide arm wins here too, rule out head count before
concluding anything about reuse.
INSTRUMENT WARNING: the output alphabet is UNARY (')' only). A model
emitting only ')' scores byte accuracy 1.0 whenever true depth is 1, so byte
accuracy alone cannot separate a right answer from a right length by luck.
Decisive readouts are length_exact_rate and mean_len_ratio WITH byte accuracy
beside them. The floor here is NOT 0.333 -- it is what a length-only
guesser emitting the training-set modal depth scores. Compute it from the
eval set first; nothing in this manifest makes that automatic.
eval_max_new stays at the inherited 16, which is sufficient: the target is
")".repeat(depth) and depth is capped at 3 (Track A) / 6 (Track B), so no
target exceeds 6 characters. The INPUT reaches 28 characters, which is the
length gradient being probed.
auto_batch stays OFF so the arms differ only in reuse pattern.
STEP BUDGET IS 2000, not the 600 the other architecture arms used.
Raised deliberately, and this is the one place a number here is NOT
comparable to the compute-matched / params-free / frontier results: those
ran 600 steps, and the gate-structure experiment showed 600 is short. At 600
the 1-gate arm read held-out 0.748 and at 2000 it read 0.891, with its
in-distribution exact-match going 0.541 -> 0.805. A rung measured at 600 and
a rung measured at 2000 are different cells, and comparing across them
would repeat the undertrained-pass error this repo has already retracted
once. So the dyck1 pair is internally consistent (both arms 2000) and
externally scoped to itself. See research/findings.md.
BATCH IS 64, PINNED EXPLICITLY, and this is the largest value both arms can
run identically. Measured on the idle card: at batch 64 this arm peaks at
2751MB of 4096MB, while the wide arm peaks at 605MB. Batch 128 would predict
>4GB for the looping arm, so 64 is the ceiling for a value BOTH arms share.
Why pin it rather than turn on auto_batch: the two arms have different
d_model (128 vs 64) and therefore different activation footprints, so the
tuner would hand them different realized batches -- which is precisely the
confound that ruined the first frontier pass (see research/AGENTS.md
contract 10). Equal and explicit beats tuned and different.
The batch-6 result this replaces was measured on an underused card: 64 rows
of ~28 characters is a small amount of work per step. Both arms are re-run at
64 here, so the comparison stays paired and the earlier numbers are superseded
rather than compared against.
MICRO_BT_BUDGET 3072, EXPLICIT, and this is the knob that matters — not
`batch_size`. Measured:
budget 2048 (shipped) : 32 rows/micro, ~1405MB of 4096MB
budget 3072            : 48 rows/micro, 3247MB  <- this
budget 4096            : OOM, 'can't allocate buffer of size 61771776'
`train.batch_size` does NOT control how many rows reach the GPU. The loop
trims each micro to `budget / padded_T`, and dyck1 pads to the shortest
band (64), so at the shipped 2048 every micro is 32 rows whatever
`batch_size` says — 64, 128, 256 and 512 all trained identical work and
all read ~1405MB. `batch_size` is the accumulation target; the budget is
the micro size. That is why the first pass of this rung looked like it was
using 4% of the card.
WHY EXPLICIT RATHER THAN `auto_batch: true`, which also raises the budget:
the tuner sizes each arm independently from measured memory, so arms with
different d_model get different realized batches. Measured here: looping
would get effective 64 and wide effective 128 — precisely the confound that
invalidated the first frontier pass. One explicit budget gives both arms
the same 48-row micro.
per_cell is 400 (not 200) so a 48-row micro is a real sample of a 1200-
instance pool rather than 4% of a 400-instance one. Both arms share it, so
the held-out split is identical across arms.
Run:
cargo run --example scaling_sweep -- \
research/experiments/arch-dyck1-looping.json depth gpu 8 \
